newsitem.title: CHINA: China B share firms to post poor 1996 results.
newsitem.headline: China B share firms to post poor 1996 results.

text.p: China's foreign currency B share firms are expected to post disappointing results for last year, but marking a slight improvement on 1995, analysts said on Friday.
The companies, many dogged by poor management and heavy debts, benefited from two interest rate cuts last year but a full recovery is unlikely until the second half of 1997, the analysts said.
Only two of the 86 companies with B shares listed in Shanghai and Shenzhen have so far released their 1996 results.

"I believe we will see slightly better results in 1996 due to the improved economy," said one broker. "But there will be no big leap forward because the improvement in the performance of listed firms has lagged behind the economy."
Shanghai's B share companies as a whole saw a reversal in fortunes in 1994 and 1995, but analysts polled said they saw a slight improvement for 1996.

"It would be hard for 1996 to be much worse," said an analyst with a western brokerage in Shanghai. "I think the results will still be awful, but quite a number of companies will be reporting better earnings."

China's economy improved last year with retail inflation falling to a year-on-year 6.1 percent in 1996 from a year-on-year 14.8 percent in 1995, prompting Beijing to cut bank interest rates in May and again in August.

One of the major disasters of the 1995 reporting season was Shanghai Tyre and Rubber Co, which posted a 92 percent fall in net profit, but brokers and the company itself now express cautious optimism.
"With prices of raw materials falling and market conditions better due to the improved economy, we expect much better results for 1996 than 1995," said a Tyre and Rubber spokesman.
Analysts said companies expected to continue to post poor results included textile machinery makers Shanghai Erfangji Co and China Textile Machinery Co.
A spokesman for Erfangji agreed that the company expected no improvement in its 1996 performance.
A company official at Shanghai Yaohua Pilkington Glass Co, which posted strong results in 1993 and 1994, also said his company expected dire earnings due to fierce competition.

But a number of other major firms in Shanghai including Shanghai Chlor Alkali Chemical Co, Shanghai Dazhong Taxi Co and Shanghai Diesel Engine Co said they would post steady increases in after-tax profits for 1996.
Companies listed in the second half of last year expected strong results because China was setting higher standards for listing companies than previously, analysts said.
These firms include Inner Mongolia Erdos Cashmere Products Co, Heilongjiang Eletric Power Co and Eastern Communications Co.
An analyst with a European brokerage said he expected Shenzhen B share companies to post stronger performances than Shanghai. "Shenzhen companies tend to be more entrepreneurial," he said.
But the investors and brokerages are looking to 1997 as the year of real recovery as the economy improves.
"I'm encouraged," said a western broker. "Last year we said that things would get better. Now things really are getting better."
